questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: Why does Mutahhari describe Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin as the ‘champion of spirituality’?
questions.answer: Mutahhari uses this description because Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin embodied the inner reality of Islam through profound faith, worship, and closeness to God. His spirituality was not merely an outward religious appearance or a set of bodily actions. His prayers and devotion reflected a soul deeply absorbed in the remembrance of Allah. Mutahhari says that when one observes Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin, one sees the reality of Islam as it had penetrated the Household of the Prophet. The Imam is therefore presented as an outstanding example of spiritual life in its true sense.
questions.source_locator: Opening discussion — Spirituality embodied in the Prophet’s Household

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: How does Mutahhari connect Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin’s spirituality with the wider spirituality of the Prophet’s Household?
questions.answer: Mutahhari says that Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin’s spiritual character should be understood as part of a quality shared by the Household of the Prophet. He points especially to Imam ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was raised by the Prophet from childhood and remained exceptionally close to him. By observing ‘Ali’s faith and devotion, one can see the depth of the Prophet’s influence. Mutahhari asks what could produce such complete faith in a person who knew the Prophet so intimately. He then says that the same spiritual reality is visible in Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin and the other members of the Prophet’s Household.
questions.source_locator: Opening discussion — Spirituality embodied in the Prophet’s Household

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: How does Mutahhari distinguish Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin’s worship from merely performing the outward movements of prayer?
questions.answer: Mutahhari explains that the Imam’s worship was marked by complete inward absorption in God. His body might be standing before the Ka‘bah, but his soul was not distracted by other concerns. He cites the description of worship as a journey of the soul toward Allah and says that when one observes the Imam, it is as though one sees the Prophet in the mihrab during the final part of the night. The Imam’s prayer was therefore not simply a physical performance; it expressed a deep spiritual state in which his attention and inner being were directed toward God.
questions.source_locator: The Imam’s acts of worship

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: What incident involving one of Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin’s children illustrates the depth of his absorption in worship?
questions.answer: One night, while the Imam was engaged in his usual worship, one of his children fell and broke a bone. The family brought a bone-setter and treated the child’s injury while the child cried out in pain. They did not interrupt the Imam because he was so absorbed in worship that the surrounding sounds did not reach him. The next morning, he noticed the child’s bandaged hand and asked what had happened. When the family explained the incident, it became clear that he had not heard the child’s cries. Mutahhari uses the story to illustrate the extraordinary depth of the Imam’s concentration and devotion to Allah.
questions.source_locator: The Imam’s acts of worship

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: Why was Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin known as the ‘herald of affection’?
questions.answer: He was known by this description because he actively sought out people who were isolated, unknown, poor, or overlooked by society. Rather than waiting for them to approach him, he showed them affection, invited them to his home, and treated them with kindness. Mutahhari emphasizes that the Imam’s concern extended to people whom others often avoided or ignored. His affection was therefore practical and personal: he gave attention and care to those who had little social status or support.
questions.source_locator: The herald of affection

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: What did Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin do when he encountered a group of people with leprosy?
questions.answer: Mutahhari says that when the Imam saw a group of people with leprosy, he invited them to his home and personally cared for them. He notes that people often feel repelled by those with leprosy because of an exaggerated fear of infection, but the Imam recognized them as servants of Allah who deserved dignity and compassion. The incident illustrates that his affection was not selective or limited to people who were socially accepted. He treated even those whom society avoided with kindness and hospitality.
questions.source_locator: The herald of affection

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: Why did Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin choose to travel with a Hajj caravan whose members did not know who he was?
questions.answer: The Imam wanted to serve the travellers without the special treatment that would follow if they recognized him as the grandson of the Prophet. He deliberately joined a caravan from a distant area, presented himself as an ordinary young man, and asked whether he could help them. He knew from experience that people who recognized his status would not allow him to serve them. By travelling with strangers, he could perform acts of service freely and gain the spiritual benefit of helping Muslims and fellow travellers.
questions.source_locator: The service in the Hajj caravan

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: How long did the journey to Mecca usually take for the Hajj caravan described by Mutahhari?
questions.answer: Mutahhari says that in those days people commonly travelled to Mecca by camel or horseback, and the journey usually took about ten to twelve days. During this period, Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin served the caravan as an ordinary traveller. The detail helps show that his service was not a brief gesture but a sustained act of humility and practical care throughout the journey.
questions.source_locator: The service in the Hajj caravan

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: How did the members of the Hajj caravan react when they discovered that their fellow traveller was Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin?
questions.answer: When a person who knew the Imam recognized him and revealed his identity to the caravan, the travellers were shocked and felt ashamed that they had allowed the grandson of the Prophet to serve them. They rushed toward him, apologized, and asked him to stop serving them and allow them to serve him instead. The Imam refused to change his arrangement. He explained that he had deliberately chosen a caravan whose members did not know him because people who recognized him would not permit him to serve them. His response shows that he valued service more than the honour normally attached to his status.
questions.source_locator: The service in the Hajj caravan

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: What does Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin’s service in the Hajj caravan teach about humility and religious leadership?
questions.answer: The episode shows that the Imam did not regard service as beneath his dignity. Although he was the grandson of the Prophet, he deliberately travelled without revealing his identity so that he could help ordinary Muslims. He preferred the opportunity to serve others over receiving honour or special treatment. Mutahhari uses the story to show that true spiritual greatness is expressed through humility and practical service, not through demanding deference from others. The Imam’s leadership was visible in his willingness to serve people rather than place himself above them.
questions.source_locator: The service in the Hajj caravan

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: Why does Mutahhari say that Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin’s prayers were an important form of service to Islam?
questions.answer: Mutahhari explains that Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin did not have the same opportunity for public armed resistance that had been available to Imam al-Husayn, nor the same intellectual opening that later existed for Imam al-Sadiq. However, a person who sincerely wishes to serve Islam can find other forms of service according to the circumstances. The Imam created an enduring honour for the Shi‘ah community through his prayers and supplications. His worship became a means of preserving and expressing the spiritual message of Islam when other forms of public action were restricted.
questions.source_locator: The Imam’s prayers and tear shedding

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: Why does Mutahhari reject the claim that Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin allowed Imam al-Husayn’s message to be forgotten because he did not rise with the sword?
questions.answer: Mutahhari says that the Imam used every opportunity available to keep the memory of his father’s martyrdom alive. His constant mourning was not simply uncontrolled personal grief. It reminded people of why Imam al-Husayn had risen, the injustice he opposed, and those responsible for his martyrdom. By preserving the memory of Karbala through tears and prayer, Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin continued the mission of his father in a form suited to his circumstances. His lack of armed revolt therefore did not mean that he abandoned resistance or allowed the message of Karbala to disappear.
questions.source_locator: The Imam’s prayers and tear shedding

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: Explain how Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin’s worship demonstrates spirituality as an inward reality rather than an outward religious performance.
questions.answer: Mutahhari presents Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin as a champion of spirituality because his worship reflected complete inward absorption in Allah. His prayer was not merely the body standing before the Ka‘bah while the mind wandered elsewhere; it was a journey of the soul toward God. Mutahhari compares the experience of observing the Imam with seeing the Prophet in worship during the final part of the night. The story of the child who broke his hand illustrates the point: the family treated the injury while the Imam was so absorbed in worship that he did not hear the cries. The next morning he noticed the bandage and asked what had happened. Mutahhari uses this incident to show that the Imam’s worship was characterized by profound concentration, reverence, and spiritual presence. His example reveals the inner reality of Islam as lived by the Prophet’s Household.
questions.source_locator: The Imam’s acts of worship

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: How did Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin express affection for the vulnerable, and what do the examples in the chapter reveal about his character?
questions.answer: Mutahhari describes Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin as the herald of affection because he actively sought out people who were isolated, strangers, poor, or overlooked by society. He did not merely speak about kindness; he invited such people to his home and personally cared for them. One example is his invitation to a group of people with leprosy, whom others often avoided. He welcomed them and tended to them as fellow servants of Allah. Mutahhari describes the Imam’s home as a house of the poor, orphans, and helpless. These examples reveal a spirituality that was not separated from human responsibility. The Imam’s closeness to God was expressed through tenderness, hospitality, and practical service to people who were often neglected.
questions.source_locator: The herald of affection

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: Explain the significance of Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin’s decision to serve an unfamiliar Hajj caravan rather than travel with people who knew his identity.
questions.answer: The Imam deliberately chose a caravan from a distant region whose members did not recognize him. He joined them as an ordinary traveller and asked whether he could serve them during the journey, which usually lasted ten to twelve days. When a person who knew him revealed his identity, the travellers were ashamed and asked him to stop serving them. The Imam refused, explaining that people who knew his status would not allow him to serve them. His decision shows that he sought the spiritual benefit of serving others rather than the social honour of being recognized. Mutahhari uses the story to demonstrate humility: true leadership is not measured by how many people serve the leader, but by the leader’s willingness to serve others.
questions.source_locator: The service in the Hajj caravan

questions.unit_title: Chapter 3: A Discourse on Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin
questions.prompt: How did Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin use prayer and mourning to preserve the message of Karbala?
questions.answer: Mutahhari explains that Imam Zayn al-‘Abidin did not have the same opportunity for armed resistance that his father Imam al-Husayn had, nor the same intellectual opening that later existed for Imam al-Sadiq. However, he found another way to serve Islam: through prayer, supplication, and the continual remembrance of Karbala. Mutahhari rejects the idea that the Imam’s tears were simply uncontrolled grief. The Imam mourned so that people would remember why Imam al-Husayn had risen and who had killed him. When a servant asked whether it was time to stop crying, the Imam compared his grief to the grief of Prophet Ya‘qub for Yusuf, then said that he had seen eighteen “Yusufs” fall before his eyes. The mourning therefore preserved the memory and moral message of Karbala for the community.
questions.source_locator: The Imam’s prayers and tear shedding
